subject: Science
title: Independent vs. Dependent Variables — Step by Step
tipLine: One question sorts these out almost every time — this walks through it.

vocabTerms.definition: the thing a researcher deliberately changes on purpose
the outcome that's measured, which may change because of the independent variable

blocks.heading: One question decides it
blocks.body: Ask: "What did the researcher deliberately change on purpose?" That's the independent variable. Then ask: "What did they measure to see if it made a difference?" That's the dependent variable. Anything the researcher kept the same on purpose (soil type, room temperature, plant type) isn't a variable at all — it's a controlled condition.

blocks.heading: Worked example
blocks.body: "A teacher gives three groups of students different amounts of study time (20, 40, or 60 minutes) before the same quiz, then compares quiz scores." What was deliberately changed? Study time — that's independent. What was measured as the outcome? Quiz scores — that's dependent.

blocks.question: A researcher waters identical bean plants with 3 different amounts of water each week, then measures how tall each plant grows after a month. What is the independent variable?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — the amount of water is what the researcher deliberately changed on purpose.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Close — that one is either the measured outcome or something held constant. The independent variable is what was deliberately changed: the water amount.
